messages.subject: getting service times from a vector
parts:
Hi,

I have generated a vector of service times but i am not being able to maintain a global variable to return me the next value of the vector as service times.

I have managed to use the set_attribute function to set the delay time but is there a more simpler way to do it?

Regards,

Salman Memon

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] getting service times from a vector
parts:
2018-03-01 13:07 GMT+01:00 salman anis <1reach...@gmail.com>:
> Hi,
>
> I have generated a vector of service times but i am not being able to
> maintain a global variable to return me the next value of the vector as
> service times.

If you define something like

consume <- function(x) {
i <- 0
function() {
i <<- i + 1
x[[i]]
}
}

Then you can write

trajectorystd <-
trajectory("Standard path") %>%
set_attribute("start_time", consume(servicetime)) %>%
seize("STD") %>%
timeout(function() get_attribute(envs, "start_time")) %>%
release("STD")

And with the next release, in a few days, you will be able to replace

timeout(function() get_attribute(envs, "start_time"))

with

timeout_from_attribute("start_time")

>
> I have managed to use the set_attribute function to set the delay time but
> is there a more simpler way to do it?

There will be in future releases. Keep an eye on issue #123:

https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/123
